lead: Santa Ana is one of the most crowded cities in California, with older homes that see heavy daily use. Worn pipes, slab leaks and mobile home leaks cause most of its water damage.
risk: aging plumbing, slab leaks and mobile home leaks
risk_short: aging pipes, slab leaks, mobile homes
why: About 74% of Santa Ana homes were built before 1980, from the historic houses of Floral Park and French Park to the postwar tracts that fill most of the city. Many homes hold more people than they were built for, so pipes, drains and water heaters get heavy use. Cast-iron drains crack, supply lines wear thin and slab pipes start to leak after 50 or 60 years.

Santa Ana also has a lot of mobile home parks, which hold about 5% of all homes. In a mobile home, the water lines run under the floor, and a slow drip can rot the subfloor before anyone sees it. Rain is rare, but winter storms can be heavy. Low streets and older storm drains near the Santa Ana River and Santiago Creek can flood in a big downpour.
image_alt: Plumber's hands fitting pipes under a sink
image_caption: Many Santa Ana homes still run on plumbing that is 50 years old or more.
problems: Postwar homes in Wilshire Square, Morrison Park
Older homes in Floral Park, French Park
tips: Have old cast-iron drains scoped with a camera.
Check under a mobile home for drips and soft spots twice a year.
Replace a water heater that is 10 to 12 years old.
Check your meter with every tap off to catch hidden leaks.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Floral Park, French Park, Washington Square, Wilshire Square, Morrison Park, South Coast Metro and Logan, plus Tustin, Orange and Garden Grove.

faq.q: Who fixes a leak in a Santa Ana mobile home park?
faq.a: It depends on where the leak is. The park usually owns the water line up to your home's connection, and you own the plumbing under and inside the home. Check your lease or park rules. DryFlare can dry the subfloor and walls no matter who pays for the pipe repair.
